doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learning by mistakes and the first mono console in Hackensack
summary: He learned by making mistakes and describes the early six or eight channel mono console.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well then how did you learn to record?
How did I learn the whole process?
But you had to build your own equipment.
Well I didn’t build my own recording machine; I never got that far. But later on the consoles got beyond the tubes, and into components and solid-state components, so that was beyond home fixing.
But from the beginning you just had to adapt.

I would get whatever I could afford, what was available to use for the recording machine: the console, and the…this is just an audio medium now. The first console had one meter in it, just one meter to do everything. Mix it down to mono, not stereo; this is in Hackensack, early Hackensack. Then we make the master mono.
How many channels coming into the console?
Which means you had six or eight microphones.
Which meant six or eight knobs; count the knobs. I did a lot of re-dos like that too.
